added_failures_note: Derived from source baseline_suite and after_suite logs and cross-checked against receipt failure IDs; zero added failures.

assertion_analysis.fails_if: Sweep skips or duplicates a dispatched launch, or returns a refusal instead of a dispatched receipt.
Real review dispatch loses the source session or emits a non-review pointer.
An event is published before the post-dispatch tick; both polls are independently required to equal the literal empty list.
Classifier fails to classify the synthetic working worker; this is a fixture precondition, not proof of event publication.
Restoring the original recorded_fleet drops the working event; recorded base negative control shows 0 != 1.
The working event uses the wrong baseline or is emitted as inventory rather than a transition.
The subscriber suppresses the event, attaches it to the wrong source or review, or loses its in-review presentation; the expected source identity comes from the independent source pointer.
The station or subscriber leaks the owner review event to a different session.
The subscriber repeats the delivered event without another publication.
A quiet station tick regenerates a launch already recorded in its fleet image.
Sweep idempotency produces a second dispatched receipt or worker launch.
The existing working pointer is not classified working; this checks the control is populated.
Removing the raw-is-None inventory distinction causes the startup working run to generate an event.

assertion_independence: No vacuous same-input equality found. State and pointer assertions test classifier/dispatch preconditions; durability rests on independent persisted-event count, subscriber delivery and startup silence. Reinstating the recorded defect leaves the phase input unchanged and reddens line 98.
